decision.explanation: The augmented matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix}1&3&2\\3&9&6\end{bmatrix}\). Applying \(R_2\leftarrow R_2-3R_1\) gives row echelon form \(\begin{bmatrix}1&3&2\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}\). Thus y is free and x=2-3y, so option a gives the general solution.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 3x+9y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 9 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 9 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 3x+9y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 9 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 9 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Applying R₂ ← R₂ + 3R₁ gives row echelon form \(\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&3\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}\). The remaining equation is x−y=3, so x=3+y with y any real number. This is option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-y=3.
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3+y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-10y=-5 \\ 2x-4y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=4$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=4,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-10y=-5 \\ 2x-4y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=4$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=4,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-6y=10 \\ -x+3y=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=5.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-6y=10 \\ -x+3y=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=5.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/3, then R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁. This gives row echelon form \(\begin{bmatrix}1&3&-1\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}\). Hence x+3y=−1, so x=−3y−1 with y any real number. This is option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3y-1,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3y-1 \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3y-1 \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3y-1,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3y-1 \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3y-1 \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
